title: Act before you feel ready: speak up, ask, price and present

say: Act before you feel ready: speak up, ask, price and present.
This is the video for module three of Confidence Building and Self-Belief.
When you avoid something you fear, you feel relief. But that relief makes the fear stronger next time.
For example, Joy works at a bank branch in Abuja and never speaks in team meetings. She builds a fear ladder, rating each step from 0 to 10 for anxiety.

panel.heading: Joy climbs one step at a time
items: Step 1: say good morning to everyone

say: Step one, rated 2: say good morning as the meeting starts. Step two, rated 3: ask one short question.

panel.heading: Joy climbs one step at a time
items: Step 1: say good morning to everyone

say: Later steps: share one idea she has written down beforehand, then give a two-minute update on her figures. She spends one to two weeks on each step.

panel.heading: Joy climbs one step at a time
items: Step 1: say good morning to everyone

say: Step four, once rated 6, now feels like a 2. Her manager asks her to lead the proposal.
Before each step, write what you fear will happen. Afterwards, write what really happened. Usually reality is kinder.

panel.heading: Joy climbs one step at a time
items: Step 1: say good morning to everyone
panel.rule: Courage comes first. Confidence grows after you act.

say: Passive speech says, your needs matter and mine do not. It leads to resentment.

panel.heading: Passive or assertive?

say: Assertive speech says, my needs and yours both matter. It is clear and respectful.
Use an I statement. I feel stressed when payment comes late, because I need it to buy materials. Can we agree on payment by the 5th?

panel.heading: Passive or assertive?

say: For example, Patience, a caterer in Benin City, supplied small chops worth about 85,000 naira. The client has delayed the balance for three weeks. She plans the call with DESC.

panel.heading: DESC: Patience asks for her balance
items: Express: I have already paid my suppliers
Specify: please pay the balance by Friday
Consequences: steady prices, or two dates

say: Describe the facts without blame. I delivered on 12 October. 40,000 naira has been paid and 45,000 is outstanding.

panel.heading: DESC: Patience asks for her balance
items: Express: I have already paid my suppliers
Specify: please pay the balance by Friday
Consequences: steady prices, or two dates

say: Express how it affects you. I am concerned because I have already paid my suppliers.

panel.heading: DESC: Patience asks for her balance
items: Express: I have already paid my suppliers
Specify: please pay the balance by Friday
Consequences: steady prices, or two dates

say: Specify one clear change. Please can you pay the balance by Friday?

panel.heading: DESC: Patience asks for her balance
items: Express: I have already paid my suppliers
Specify: please pay the balance by Friday
Consequences: steady prices, or two dates

say: Consequences. That way I can keep my prices steady. If it is difficult, let us agree on two dates today.
He pays within two weeks. To say no, calmly repeat your main message without new excuses. I am not able to lend money this month.

panel.heading: DESC: Patience asks for her balance
items: Express: I have already paid my suppliers
Specify: please pay the balance by Friday
Consequences: steady prices, or two dates

say: Many women undercharge because asking for more feels greedy. A fair price covers your costs, your time and a reasonable profit.
For example, Rukayat is asked to sew 20 aso-ebi outfits. The client supplies the fabric.
Thread, lining and accessories cost about 2,500 naira per outfit. Transport and electricity add about 1,000.
Each outfit takes about 4 hours, and she values her labour at 1,500 naira an hour. That is 6,000.
So cost plus labour is about 9,500 naira per outfit. Other tailors nearby charge 12,000 to 15,000 naira.
Before she speaks, she decides three numbers. Ideal, 14,000. Target, 12,500. Walk-away point, 10,000.

panel.heading: Three numbers, then pause
items: Say it once, clearly, then wait
Lower only for something in return

say: She says, for 20 outfits in this style, my price is 14,000 naira each, ready in three weeks. Then she waits.

panel.heading: Three numbers, then pause
items: Say it once, clearly, then wait
Lower only for something in return

say: The family offers 11,000. She replies, I can do 12,500 if you pay 60 percent upfront and confirm measurements by Saturday. They agree.

panel.heading: Three numbers, then pause
items: Say it once, clearly, then wait
Lower only for something in return

say: Never price below cost to please a client. And watch for fake transfer alerts. Confirm payment in your actual bank app before releasing goods, and never share your BVN, PIN or OTP.

panel.heading: Three numbers, then pause
items: Say it once, clearly, then wait
Lower only for something in return
panel.rule: Never price below cost. Confirm payment in your app first.

say: Build every talk around one main idea. For example, Chinwe, a cooperative treasurer in Onitsha, wants members to save in a group bank account.
She opens with a hook. Last year, two of our members lost their savings to fire and theft.

panel.heading: A short talk in three parts

cards.d: Greet, then a short story, question or fact. About 30 seconds.
Each point with an example. About 2 minutes.
Repeat the main idea and say what you want people to do.

say: Then three points: safety, records, and loans.

panel.heading: A short talk in three parts

cards.d: Greet, then a short story, question or fact. About 30 seconds.
Each point with an example. About 2 minutes.
Repeat the main idea and say what you want people to do.

say: She closes: let us vote today to open a group account.
She practises four times from a card of nine keywords. Her hands shake for the first minute, then settle, and the members vote yes.

cards.d: Greet, then a short story, question or fact. About 30 seconds.

Repeat the main idea and say what you want people to do.

say: To remember. Act before you feel ready, one step at a time. Speak with I statements and plan hard talks with DESC. Know your numbers before you negotiate. And build each talk around one idea.
If speaking up could put you at risk of violence, your safety comes first. Involve trusted people, and in an emergency call 112.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Climb a fear ladder, one step at a time
I feel, when, because, I would like
Know cost, target and walk-away price

say: Now build your fear ladder and climb one step, plan one DESC conversation, prepare your STAR stories and prices, and give a short talk.
Continue with the lessons below.
